_comment: Project-level Claude Code settings for THIS repo (claude-dotfiles).
NOT the mirror at claude/settings.json - that one is a GENERATED copy of
~/.claude/settings.json and is wiped on every sync push. This file is
hand-written, committed to the repo, and loaded by Claude Code when a
session starts anywhere under this checkout.
Wires the dotfiles-freshness loop (issue 12) - see tools/dotfiles-freshness.ps1
and tools/dotfiles-freshness-hook.js. Runs only for sessions in this repo,
which is where the freshness of ~/.claude vs origin actually matters.
extraKnownMarketplaces + enabledPlugins make cloud sessions (claude.ai/code)
install the aac-skills plugin from this repo at startup. Two other routes were
tried and do not work: the claude.ai account-level plugin sync returns zero
plugins for this account (plugins_sync_no_changes count:0 in the session diag
log), and the cloud environment setup script runs before the session's git
credentials exist, so cloning a private marketplace fails there. Declaring it
here is the documented path and the one verified 2026-09-09: Claude Code clones
the marketplace itself after credentials are wired up, loads all 56 skills and
runs the plugin's SessionStart hook. Not reproduced 2026-09-11: that session's
installed_plugins.json was empty (evidence on issue 106).
.claude/hooks/session-start.sh runs first on SessionStart and only in a cloud
container (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true): installs gh so the session has the same
GitHub instrument a local one has. Only `gh api` works through the cloud proxy;
GraphQL-backed gh commands return 403 there (issue 130).
permissions.defaultMode is acceptEdits per the issue 170 ruling (Dan,
2026-09-14): cloud sessions run under lever 1 - Accept edits with a blanket
Bash allow list, not auto mode. Accept edits pre-approves edits, honours the
allow list (auto mode drops Bash(*)) and skips the classifier that denied
ordinary ~/.claude reads as Data Exfiltration in probe cse_01RQ89qFjEiXXmd1hgooqFBV.
Cost: an unattended agent has unrestricted shell inside the container, bounded
only by the security/GitHub proxy and the repo scope. permissions.allow keeps
Bash(*), WebFetch, WebSearch and mcp__github__* so nothing prompts.
